record.original_question: Generalize domain wall boundary conditions from the six-vertex model to other integrable models in such a way that the partition function retains the key determinant property: it should be representable as a determinant whose dimension is proportional to the size of the system.

evidence.quote: Using the recursion relations Izergin was able to derive a determinantal formula for the partition function.
The main feature of formula (19) is the fact that the partition function of the six vertex model with DWBC is expressed as a determinant of the size of the system.

Open problem: Obtain generalizations of domain wall boundary conditions for other models such that the partition function is expressed as a determinant of a dimension proportional with the size of the system.

artifact.category_tag: six-vertex model and domain wall boundary conditions
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The six-vertex model on an N×N square lattice assigns to each edge an arrow (one of two orientations) subject to the ice rule that at every internal vertex exactly two arrows point in and two point out, giving six allowed local configurations with Boltzmann weights a, b, c. Domain wall boundary conditions (DWBC) fix all horizontal external edges to point inward and all vertical external edges to point outward (or a consistent rotation thereof). Under DWBC, the partition function Z_N satisfies recursion relations (due to Korepin) that uniquely determine it, and Izergin showed that Z_N admits a closed-form representation as an N×N determinant (the Izergin–Korepin determinant), i.e. a determinant whose dimension is proportional to the linear size of the system.

Problem. Identify and construct analogues of domain wall boundary conditions for other integrable lattice models — for instance, higher-spin or higher-rank vertex models (such as the nineteen-vertex model, IRF/SOS models, the eight-vertex model, or vertex models associated with general quantum affine algebras U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{g}})) — such that the resulting partition function on an N×N (or otherwise linearly-sized) lattice admits an exact representation as the determinant of a matrix whose dimension grows only linearly (i.e. is proportional to N) with the system size. Specify the boundary conditions explicitly, derive the corresponding determinantal formula, and verify that it reduces, in the appropriate limits, to the Izergin–Korepin determinant of the six-vertex model.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding DWBC-like boundary conditions for general integrable models whose partition function reduces to a determinant of size linear in the system remains generally open. Partial generalizations exist (e.g. for certain higher-spin vertex models, the trigonometric/elliptic SOS models, and some boundary/reflecting variants), often yielding sums of determinants or determinants of larger size rather than the desired linear-dimension single determinant. No general construction is known.

status_evidence.title: Izergin–Korepin determinant (Wikipedia / standard references)
status_evidence.snippet: Izergin derived a determinantal formula for the partition function of the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The Izergin–Korepin determinant is specific to the six-vertex model with DWBC; analogous compact determinant formulas for other integrable models are not generally available.

status_evidence.title: Partition function of the elliptic SOS model with DWBC (Rosengren)
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizations of DWBC to SOS/elliptic models yield more complicated expressions (sums of determinants), not single determinants of linear size.
status_evidence.claim: Known generalizations typically do not preserve the single linear-size determinant property, indicating the problem is still open in general.
